title: Southern Tang
capsule: The Southern Tang (南唐, Nán Táng) was one of the Ten Kingdoms of the Five Dynasties period, ruling the lower Yangtze and Huai river basins from its capital at Jinling (modern Nanjing) after Li Bian declared himself emperor in 937 following the collapse of the Wu kingdom. Li Yu (r. 961–975), the last ruler, is celebrated as one of China's greatest lyric poets but proved a disastrous administrator who allowed the Song military to overrun the kingdom; Song forces under Zhao Kuangyi besieged Jinling for two years before the city surrendered in 975. Li Yu was taken to Kaifeng, where he died in captivity in 978, and the Southern Tang's territory was incorporated into the consolidated Song empire.
